syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

topics.title: The Day the River Spoke: Jahnavi's dream and the River's advice

concepts.learning_objective: Students will recall Jahnavi's wish to go to school and the reasons she was kept at home.
Students will explain how the River encouraged Jahnavi to find the courage to go to school.
Students will interpret the story's message that girls deserve the same chance to learn as boys.

topics.title: The Day the River Spoke: personification, sound words and prepositions

concepts.learning_objective: Students will explain why the River is written with a capital letter and given human qualities.
Students will identify and use the sound words from the story, such as shrieked, rustle and splashed.
Students will distinguish words like up and down used as prepositions from the same words used as adverbs.

topics.title: Try Again: King Bruce and the spider

concepts.learning_objective: Students will describe King Bruce's despair after repeated failure.
Students will recall how the spider kept climbing after every fall until it succeeded.
Students will analyse how the spider's success changes King Bruce's attitude and conveys the poem's message.

topics.title: Try Again: poetic devices and vocabulary

concepts.learning_objective: Students will identify the rhyme scheme, alliteration and repetition used in the poem.
Students will distinguish a metaphor from a simile.
Students will give the meanings of words from the poem such as pondered, toil and strive.

topics.title: Three Days to See: Helen Keller's three days

concepts.learning_objective: Students will recall what Helen Keller wished to see on each of her three imagined days of sight.
Students will explain how Helen Keller experiences nature and people through touch.
Students will evaluate Helen Keller's advice to make the most of every sense.

topics.title: Three Days to See: sensory words and modal verbs

concepts.learning_objective: Students will classify words from the text by the sense they describe.
Students will identify modal verbs and the functions they express, such as possibility, obligation and request.

topics.title: Animals, Birds, and Dr. Dolittle: Polynesia and the language of animals
topics.ncert_sections: Animals, Birds, and Dr. Dolittle, Part I

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the Cat's-food-Man and Polynesia advise Doctor Dolittle to become an animal doctor.
Describe how, according to Polynesia, animals and birds communicate with one another.

topics.title: Animals, Birds, and Dr. Dolittle: the plough horse and the Doctor's fame
topics.ncert_sections: Animals, Birds, and Dr. Dolittle, Part II

concepts.learning_objective: Recount the plough horse's problem and explain how speaking its language helped the Doctor cure it.
Explain how Doctor Dolittle cared for many kinds of animals and how his fame spread across the world.

topics.title: Dr. Dolittle: compound words, palindromes and the present perfect tense
topics.ncert_sections: Animals, Birds, and Dr. Dolittle, Let us learn

concepts.learning_objective: Classify compound words from the story as hyphenated, open or closed compounds.
Identify words and sentences that read the same backwards as forwards.
Use the present perfect tense (has/have + past participle) for actions relevant at the time of speaking.

topics.title: A Funny Man: the poem and its humour
topics.ncert_sections: A Funny Man (poem)

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the odd actions of the funny man and the poet's reactions to them.
Identify devices such as alliteration, rhyme and mixed-up sense images that create humour in the poem.

topics.title: A Funny Man: phrasal verbs and limericks
topics.ncert_sections: A Funny Man, Let us learn and Let us write

concepts.learning_objective: Use phrasal verbs such as take up, take after, take in, take over and take off with their correct meanings.
Recognise the five-line form and AABBA rhyme scheme of a limerick.

topics.title: Say the Right Thing: Mrs. Shaw's advice (Scene I)
topics.ncert_sections: Say the Right Thing, Scene I

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the advice Mrs. Shaw gives Mary about polite conversation with guests.
Infer Mary's character from her confident replies to her mother in Scene I.

topics.title: Say the Right Thing: Mary's blunders (Scene II)
topics.ncert_sections: Say the Right Thing, Scene II

concepts.learning_objective: Identify how each of Mary's remarks unknowingly offends Mrs. Harding or Mrs. Lee.
Explain how stage directions and the final line create humour in the play.

topics.title: Say the Right Thing: suffixes, tenses and kinds of sentences
topics.ncert_sections: Say the Right Thing, Let us learn

concepts.learning_objective: Form and analyse words using suffixes such as -ous, -ly, -ful, -ance and -est.
Use the present perfect continuous tense (has/have + been + verb-ing) for actions continuing up to now.
Identify declarative, interrogative, exclamatory and imperative sentences and punctuate them correctly.

topics.title: My Brother's Great Invention: the burglar alarm and the time machine
topics.ncert_sections: My Brother's Great Invention, Part I

concepts.learning_objective: Recall and explain the main events of Part I, from the burglar alarm to the time machine.
Understand the meaning of key words such as 'tinkering' as used in the story.
Compare how Anita sees Anand with how Anand sees himself, using evidence from the text.

topics.title: My Brother's Great Invention: the night of the intruder
topics.ncert_sections: My Brother's Great Invention, Part II

concepts.learning_objective: Recall and sequence the events of the night Boppa entered the house.
Infer characters' motives and the meaning of the story's open ending.

topics.title: Words in the story: onomatopoeia, binomials, idioms and phrasal verbs
topics.ncert_sections: Let us learn I-III (My Brother's Great Invention)

concepts.learning_objective: Identify onomatopoeic sound words used in the story.
Recognise binomials and use them in their fixed order and meaning.
Use idioms and phrasal verbs from the story correctly in new contexts.

topics.title: Simple past and past perfect; words ending in -ough
topics.ncert_sections: Let us learn IV and Let us speak (My Brother's Great Invention)

concepts.learning_objective: Use the past perfect for the earlier of two past actions and the simple past for the later one.
Distinguish the different pronunciations of words ending in -ough.

topics.title: Paper Boats: meaning and theme of the poem
topics.ncert_sections: Paper Boats (Rabindranath Tagore)

concepts.learning_objective: Recall what the speaker does with his paper boats and what he imagines.
Interpret the theme and images of the poem, such as the fairies of sleep.

topics.title: Paper Boats: poetic devices and vocabulary
topics.ncert_sections: Paper Boats: Let us discuss and Let us learn

concepts.learning_objective: Identify alliteration, imagery and symbols in the poem.
Match words from the poem with their opposites and group words for parts of the day.

topics.title: North, South, East, West: Shaana's postcards
topics.ncert_sections: North, South, East, West (C.G. Salamander)

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the places Shaana visits and how her feelings change during the journey.
Interpret Shaana's observations about India's landscapes and environmental change.
Evaluate why the author tells the journey through postcards.

topics.title: Subject-verb agreement
topics.ncert_sections: Let us learn IV-V (North, South, East, West)

concepts.learning_objective: Choose the verb for subjects such as 'a pair of', subjects ending in -s and indefinite pronouns.
Make the verb agree with the nearer subject when subjects are joined by 'or' or 'nor'.
Keep subject and verb in agreement when other words come between them.

topics.title: The Tunnel (Part I): Suraj and the steam engine
topics.ncert_sections: The Tunnel, Part I: Let us read

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the imagery and figures of speech Ruskin Bond uses to describe the train, the tunnel and the jungle.
Explain what Suraj does at the tunnel and what it shows about his curious, adventurous nature.

topics.title: The Tunnel (Part I): Sunder Singh, the watchman
topics.ncert_sections: The Tunnel, Part I: Let us read, Let us discuss

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the watchman's day and night system for inspecting the tunnel and warning the engine driver.
Infer Sunder Singh's character from what he says about his tunnel, the jungle and the town.

topics.title: The Tunnel (Part II): The leopard and the night mail
topics.ncert_sections: The Tunnel, Part II: Let us read, Let us think and reflect

concepts.learning_objective: Recall and explain how Sunder Singh and Suraj drive the leopard out of the tunnel before the night mail.
Interpret the ending of the story and why Sunder Singh is called a 'firefly'.

topics.title: The Tunnel: sound words, 'would' and 'used to', colon and semicolon
topics.ncert_sections: The Tunnel: Let us learn I-IV

concepts.learning_objective: Match sound words from the story with their meanings and use them in sentences.
Use 'would' and 'used to' correctly to describe habits and states in the past.
Use the colon and the semicolon correctly in sentences.

topics.title: Travel (poem by Edna St. Vincent Millay)
topics.ncert_sections: Travel: Let us read, Let us discuss, Let us think and reflect

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the speaker's longing for travel and the meaning of key lines of the poem.
Identify the rhyme scheme, personification and imagery used in the poem.

topics.title: Travel: words for sounds and the soft and hard 'c'
topics.ncert_sections: Travel: Let us learn II, Let us speak

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish words for related sounds such as wailing, bawling, whimpering and hollering.
Apply the rule for pronouncing the letter 'c' as a soft /s/ or a hard /k/ sound.

topics.title: Conquering the Summit: Arunima Sinha's journey
topics.ncert_sections: Conquering the Summit: Let us read, Let us discuss

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the main events of Arunima Sinha's journey from her accident to the Seven Summits.
Evaluate Arunima Sinha's message about goals, failure and resilience.

topics.title: Conquering the Summit: phrases, word forms and articles
topics.ncert_sections: Conquering the Summit: Let us learn I-III

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the meanings of phrases such as 'beacon of hope' and 'mental fortitude' in context.
Identify the noun, adjective, verb and adverb forms of words from the text.
Use the articles 'a', 'an' and 'the' correctly, and recognise where no article is needed.

topics.title: A Homage to Our Brave Soldiers: Soumya's visit to the National War Memorial

concepts.learning_objective: Recall key facts about the National War Memorial and explain why such memorials matter.
Identify India's gallantry awards and interpret the citations of the heroes named in the letter.

topics.title: The four Chakras and the Amar Jawan Jyoti

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the four concentric circles of the memorial and what each symbolises.
Explain the meaning of the Amar Jawan Jyoti and the obelisk with the eternal flame.

topics.title: Ananda's reply: gratitude and inspiration

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret Ananda's views on war memorials and our duty to honour soldiers.
Recall details of Ananda's letter such as the Chandigarh memorial and her hobby of philately.

topics.title: Let us learn: prefixes and subordinate clauses

concepts.learning_objective: Form and understand words made with prefixes such as dis-, in-, im-, un-, re- and de-.
Identify main and subordinate clauses and use subordinating conjunctions correctly.

topics.title: My Dear Soldiers (poem by A.P.J. Abdul Kalam)

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the poet, theme and tone of the poem 'My Dear Soldiers'.
Recognise and interpret poetic devices such as simile and metaphor in the poem.
Choose words that collocate naturally, as practised with the poem.

topics.title: Rani Abbakka: the queen of Ullal

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how and why Rani Abbakka defied the Portuguese.
Understand the meanings of words from the story such as vassal and defied.

topics.title: Spelling, silent letters and reported speech

concepts.learning_objective: Apply the 'ie/ei' spelling rule and recognise silent letters.
Change direct speech into indirect speech with the correct changes of tense, person, time and place.
